hero.title: AI Automation and Dynamic Routing Learning
hero.desc: Manage AI model selection, natural-language tasks, prompt templates, AI Profiles, and local dynamic-routing learning here. Settings keeps only lightweight switches so it does not load heavy task data.

result.title: Current result
result.profileReady: A switchable Profile has been prepared for this result.
result.profileNotReady: This result does not contain a new Profile output.
result.toolExecutionHint: Review tool execution and protected actions before switching runtime reads.

dispatch.title: Advanced dispatch
dispatch.desc: Keep multi-AI orchestration available without putting it on the first screen.

assets.templatesDesc: Templates, tool access, and snapshots stay here as reusable assets.

config.title: AI execution model
config.desc: Customize the AI channel, model, and base URL. Without customization, Octopus uses the local OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
config.apiKeyPlaceholder: Optional: enter a temporary API key or leave empty for the local default
config.localDefaultDesc: When no custom AI endpoint is provided, Octopus prefers the local `127.0.0.1` OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
config.activeSourceManualDesc: Runtime is currently reading manual configuration. AI-generated plans stay preserved as Profiles until you switch them on manually.
config.localDefaultHint: The default endpoint is inferred from the current service and falls back to http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1. This model is only for AI automation tasks and never changes business routing priority.
config.enabledDesc: When disabled, you can still review config, profiles, and learning state, but Octopus will not fetch models or create new AI tasks.
config.disabledHint: Enable AI automation before fetching models or creating AI tasks.

task.title: Natural-language tasks
task.desc: Ask for grouping, channel recognition, or profile generation. AI creates suggestions or Profiles and never overwrites manual configuration.
task.placeholder: Example: identify these channel types and generate a reviewable grouping Profile.
task.quickIntentsDesc: Jump into common task templates without retyping the same request.
task.dispatchControlDesc: Choose parallel or sequential dispatch first, then cap how many AI lanes may run in this launch so setup stays powerful without becoming noisy.
task.humanDefaultsDesc: The workbench prepares a sensible default stack for you first, while still leaving every knob available when you want to fine-tune.
task.laneModelDesc: Recommended models are auto-filled by default. Only override them when you want different AIs to handle different lanes.
task.laneEndpointSummaryInherited: All lanes are currently inheriting the main AI config, so you can launch immediately.
task.laneEndpointSummaryCustom: Some lanes already use dedicated endpoint / key / channel routes for multi-AI dispatch.
task.consoleDesc: Centralize context, split strategy, tool switches, lane models, and snapshots here. Current multi-AI runs fan out into frontend-launched lane tasks instead of a backend orchestrator.
task.consoleModeDesc: Stay in simple mode for most runs. Switch to advanced mode only when you need to fine-tune lanes, tools, or dedicated AI routes.
task.quickControlDesc: Keep the most common context, split, and parallelism controls here so the workbench stays strong without feeling crowded.
task.consoleHintOne: Defaults are already tuned so you can skip most setup and launch immediately.
task.consoleHintTwo: Manual config and AI-generated plans coexist; switching sources never overwrites your original data.
task.presetGalleryDesc: Start from a project-aligned preset and then fine-tune only what you need.
task.laneLaunchDesc: Planner, executor, reviewer, and guard lane tasks launched from the frontend appear here for quick inspection.
task.laneLaunchEmpty: No AI lanes launched yet. Run a split task and they will appear here.
task.diffCurrentDesc: This is the currently active or selected AI Profile content.
task.diffResultDesc: This is the newly generated task result for comparison.
task.mainChainHint: Keep the first screen focused on one task chain. Advanced dispatch, templates, history, and learning stay below as secondary workspaces.

typeDescriptions.natural_language: Best for open-ended requests where AI should digest, summarize, and structure the current context.
typeDescriptions.group_suggestion: Focused on generating grouping suggestions and AI Profile drafts without touching manual groups.
typeDescriptions.channel_recognition: Focused on identifying channel types, source traits, and model coverage.
typeDescriptions.price_recognition: Focused on inferring pricing and billing patterns, but only as suggestions without writing back pricing tables.
typeDescriptions.model_classification: Focused on model taxonomy, capability grouping, and naming organization.
typeDescriptions.config_health_check: Focused on reviewing the current configuration structure, risks, and fallback guidance.
typeDescriptions.dynamic_routing_digest: Focused on explaining dynamic routing and local learning state for manual review.

task.customPromptPlaceholder: Optional: add a custom work requirement, operator instruction, or extra constraint.
task.executionSnapshotDesc: The current page values for base URL, API key, channel type, and model are used directly for model fetch and task execution, even before saving.
task.snapshotPanelDesc: Save the current AI automation state and restore it later with one click.
task.snapshotLabelPlaceholder: Name this snapshot for easier rollback
task.snapshotEmpty: No snapshots yet. Create one as a rollback point.
task.latestSnapshotDesc: If there is no recent snapshot yet, create one before running higher-risk automation work.
task.effectiveModelDesc: By default Octopus prefers a recommended model that is likely free, healthy, and reasonably fast, while still letting you override it manually.
task.toolCapabilityDesc: These switches decide which context AI may read in this run, what kind of result it may generate, and whether protective actions are allowed.
task.laneStrategyDesc: Pick a multi-AI split strategy first, then fine-tune each lane model only if needed. Today this launches multiple independent tasks rather than a backend orchestrator graph.
task.laneEndpointDesc: Assign a dedicated AI endpoint, API key, and channel type to the planner, executor, reviewer, or guard lane. Each lane inherits the main config by default until you switch it to a custom route.
task.laneEndpointInheritHint: This lane currently reuses the main AI base URL, API key, channel type, and local-default switch.
task.laneEndpointCustomHint: This lane now uses its own channel config so different AI providers or routes can be split across roles.
task.templatePromptPlaceholder: Enter the template prompt that tells AI how to organize, recognize, or classify the target context.
task.templateRequirementPlaceholder: Optional: add work requirements, output boundaries, or prohibited actions.
task.detailInputDesc: Backup natural-language input. The main action is already above, so use this only when you need to add extra detail.
task.examplesDesc: Even if you do not want to type from scratch, you can start from an example close to the current workspace.
task.executionReceiptReadSummary: This run read {read} tool results and organized {context} context objects.
task.failureNextStep: Next step: check the execution model, templates, and natural-language examples above, then create the task again or try one-click setup.

lanePrompts.planner: Break the request into a structured execution plan and call out the context that is required.
lanePrompts.executor: Produce the main organized output and the draft AI Profile.
lanePrompts.reviewer: Review risks, gaps, conflicts, and rollback suggestions.
lanePrompts.guard: Emphasize manual-config safety, snapshot recovery, and dynamic-routing boundaries.
lanePrompts.primary: Complete the current task in a single lane.

parallel.label: Parallel dispatch
parallel.desc: Best for complex work. Multiple AI lanes start together so planning and review arrive sooner.

sequential.label: Sequential dispatch
sequential.desc: Best for careful review. Planning, execution, and review move in order so risk is easier to control.

read_context.title: Read-only analysis
read_context.desc: Let AI read channels, groups, pricing, models, and learning state to understand the current workspace.

generate_outputs.title: Generate plans
generate_outputs.desc: Let AI produce reviewable, switchable AI Profiles and structured suggestions.

protected_actions.title: Protected actions
protected_actions.desc: Only after explicit authorization may AI activate a profile, create a snapshot, or perform other guarded actions.

channel_inventory.label: Read channel inventory
channel_inventory.desc: Let AI understand the current channel, key, and source layout.

group_topology.label: Read group topology
group_topology.desc: Let AI understand the current structure from groups and group_items.

price_catalog.label: Read pricing catalog
price_catalog.desc: Let AI analyze local pricing and likely-free models.

model_catalog.label: Read model catalog
model_catalog.desc: Let AI see the current model list and auto-discovery results.

route_overrides.label: Read route overrides
route_overrides.desc: Let AI detect special route target override rules.

learning_state.label: Read learning state
learning_state.desc: Let AI explain recommendation differences with dynamic-routing samples.

profile_write.label: Generate AI Profile
profile_write.desc: Allow this task to produce a reviewable and switchable AI Profile directly.

profile_activate.label: Allow profile activation
profile_activate.desc: After manual confirmation, allow AI to activate an AI Profile directly.

snapshot_guard.label: Create config snapshot
snapshot_guard.desc: Automatically record a rollback point before higher-risk actions.

balanced_default.label: Balanced default
balanced_default.desc: Recommended starting template with planner, executor, and reviewer lanes for a good speed and safety balance.

speed_first.label: Fast draft
speed_first.desc: Compresses the flow into planner plus executor so a usable draft appears quickly.

safety_first.label: Careful review
safety_first.desc: Keeps the reviewer lane and enables snapshot protection by default before touching real configuration.

mesh_guarded.label: Fully guarded mesh
mesh_guarded.desc: Opens planner, executor, reviewer, and guard lanes for complex automation or higher-risk checks.

model_taxonomy.label: Model taxonomy mirror
model_taxonomy.desc: Prioritizes model classification, channel mapping, and free-model tendency before deeper grouping work.

hybrid_orchestrator.label: Hybrid dispatch workbench
hybrid_orchestrator.desc: Uses concurrent lane dispatch for more complex natural-language requests and future AI automation expansion.

channel_group_rollout.title: AI channel grouping rollout template
channel_group_rollout.desc: Generate a switchable plan from the current Octopus channel, group, and model structure while keeping manual configuration untouched by default.
channel_group_rollout.input: Identify the current channel types and model coverage, generate a maintainable grouping plan, and produce a reviewable, switchable AI Profile.
channel_group_rollout.prompt: Strictly preserve manual channels, groups, group_items, priority, and explicit ordering. First output the grouping principles, then the structured AI Profile and manual review checkpoints.

channel_price_rollout.title: AI channel pricing rollout template
channel_price_rollout.desc: Scan model and channel pricing signals, then output free, paid, and needs-review classifications without directly overwriting the pricing table.
channel_price_rollout.input: Identify the pricing, free-model tendency, and billing characteristics of the current channels and models, then generate a switchable pricing-recognition AI Profile.
channel_price_rollout.prompt: Do not write back to llm_infos silently. Prioritize models that are likely free, healthy, and low-latency, and mark uncertain entries as needing review.

multi_ai_dispatch_rollout.title: AI multi-model concurrent split template
multi_ai_dispatch_rollout.desc: Launch planner, executor, reviewer, and guard lane tasks together for complex automation work and larger batches of requests.
multi_ai_dispatch_rollout.input: Split this complex task into a multi-AI concurrent plan, while also handling channel recognition, grouping suggestions, risk notes, and rollback protection.
multi_ai_dispatch_rollout.prompt: Enable multi-AI dispatch, snapshot protection, and AI Profile output. Never overwrite the original manual configuration silently, and suggest manual switching when necessary.

channel_grouping.title: Channel recognition plus smart grouping workbench
channel_grouping.desc: Prioritize source organization, model coverage, and grouping drafts while keeping manual configuration untouched.
channel_grouping.input: Identify these channel types, organize them into a readable grouping structure, and generate a reviewable AI Profile.
channel_grouping.prompt: Do not overwrite existing manual groups, group_items, or priority. Output an actionable AI Profile draft and manual verification checkpoints.

price_taxonomy.title: Pricing recognition plus model taxonomy audit
price_taxonomy.desc: Focus on pricing inference, free-model priority, and model capability classification without directly editing the pricing table.
price_taxonomy.input: Identify pricing and billing characteristics, classify model capabilities, and generate a switchable AI Profile.
price_taxonomy.prompt: Output only suggestions and an AI Profile. Do not write back to llm_infos directly. Prioritize models that are free, healthy, and low-latency.

ops_guardian.title: Ops guardian plus config inspection template
ops_guardian.desc: Inspect dynamic routing, AI Profiles, and runtime configuration together, then provide risk notes and rollback guidance.
ops_guardian.input: Inspect the current AI automation state, dynamic-routing learning, and profile switching status, then provide safe rollback guidance.
ops_guardian.prompt: Focus on the coexistence of manual mode and AI Profile mode, the fact that dynamic-routing learning only affects runtime ordering, and every available recovery point.

model_taxonomy.title: Model taxonomy plus channel mirror template
model_taxonomy.desc: Organize model naming, capabilities, and channel mirrors first so the model layer becomes easier to clean up.
model_taxonomy.input: Organize model naming, capabilities, free-model tendency, and channel sources into a reviewable, switchable AI Profile.
model_taxonomy.prompt: Do not overwrite manual pricing, manual grouping, or existing priorities. Focus on model taxonomy, channel mirrors, and manual review checkpoints.

hybrid_orchestrator.title: Hybrid dispatch plus multi-AI task template
hybrid_orchestrator.desc: Designed for more complex work by letting recognition, grouping, and review run in parallel inside one multi-AI workbench as independent tasks.
hybrid_orchestrator.input: Handle channel recognition, grouping suggestions, and risk notes together, then provide a rollback-friendly multi-AI execution plan.
hybrid_orchestrator.prompt: Emphasize multi-AI dispatch, snapshot protection, and manually switchable plans. Never overwrite the original configuration silently.

routing_rehearsal.title: Dynamic routing replay plus learning review template
routing_rehearsal.desc: Purpose-built for pre-release review of dynamic-routing learning, fallback behavior, and recommendation changes.
routing_rehearsal.input: Review dynamic-routing learning state, fallback results, and recommendation changes, then output an auditable replay record.
routing_rehearsal.prompt: Explain only runtime recommendations and learning state. Do not write back to group_items, priority, or explicit ordering.

quickIntents.groupReviewText: Inspect the current channel and group structure, then summarize grouping suggestions, conflicts, and manual review points.
quickIntents.channelScanText: Identify current channel types, model coverage, and source traits, then return a structured scan.
quickIntents.priceAuditText: Check model pricing, billing mode, and likely-free status, then mark items that still need review.
quickIntents.routingDigestText: Review dynamic-routing learning, fallback outcomes, and the current recommendation order.

taskHistory.historyDesc: Saved tasks with filters and paging.

models.title: Model candidates
models.desc: Recommended for AI automation by free likelihood, success rate, and latency.
models.empty: No model candidates yet. Fetch models to organize local model and channel cache.

profiles.title: AI Profiles
profiles.desc: AI-generated grouping, channel recognition, price recognition, and model classification are saved here for review and switching without overwriting manual config.
profiles.empty: No AI Profiles yet. Generated task results will appear here later.
profiles.activeHint: When Settings is switched to AI Profile mode, runtime reads the plan associated with this active Profile first.
profiles.noActiveHint: If you want AI-generated plans to participate in runtime reads, activate a Profile here first and then switch the source in Settings.

learning.title: Dynamic routing AI learning
learning.desc: This independent dynamic-routing learning lane only affects runtime recommendation order. It never writes back group_items, channels, or user priorities.
learning.stageDesc: Dynamic routing AI learning stays beside AI automation in its own top-level area instead of being folded into Settings, so the settings screen remains lightweight.
learning.switchDesc: When disabled, existing learning data is retained but no new samples are recorded and learning does not affect scoring.
learning.presetDesc: Use one-click presets to quickly try safer, more balanced, or more aggressive learning styles without digging through settings.
learning.presetHint: Presets only change learning participation and recommendation style. They do not overwrite existing samples or user configuration.

summary.noticeEnabledReady: Learning is currently participating in runtime recommendations, and {count} sample records are ready for review.
summary.noticeEnabledEmpty: Learning is enabled, but no samples have been captured yet. Future success, failure, latency, and race outcomes will accumulate from new runtime traffic.
summary.noticeDisabledWithSamples: Learning is currently disabled. The existing {count} sample records remain available for review, but they no longer affect recommendation scoring.
summary.noticeDisabledEmpty: Learning is currently disabled and there are no samples to review yet. Re-enable learning before Octopus starts accumulating data.

learning.empty: No learning samples yet. When enabled, Octopus records success rate, failure rate, latency, and race winners by channel/key/model.
learning.resetDisabledHint: There is no learning data to reset yet.

toast.templateRequired: Enter both a template name and prompt first
toast.learningSaveFailed: Failed to save dynamic routing learning switch

detail.keyFilterHint: This field only filters keys that have already been added. It is not the input for the actual API key.
detail.keyFilterPlaceholder: Filter existing keys, remarks, source, models, or status code

mode.pooled: Keys in this channel are treated as a shared pool for the same model set.
mode.classified: Keys in this channel keep explicit model scopes and are routed within matching subsets.

policy.round_robin: Eligible keys rotate in strict order for new requests.
policy.fill_priority: Each request prefers the primary eligible key first, then falls back in order only when needed.
policy.priority_order: Every new request starts from the first eligible key and falls back in configured order.

form.name: Channel Name
form.channelProxyPlaceholder: Optional: proxy for this channel (overrides global proxy)

form.autoGroupHint: Turn this on only when you want models to be attached to existing groups automatically. For a new channel, keeping it off first is usually easier.
form.matchRegexPlaceholder: Optional: regex pattern to match request model names
form.providerPresetPlaceholder: Select a provider to auto-fill Base URL and type
form.providerPresetHint: Choose this first for common providers. It fills the base URL and channel type for you, then you can fine-tune the rest.
form.nameHint: Use a name you can recognize at a glance, such as one based on provider, account, or purpose, so later troubleshooting stays easy.
form.typeHint: The channel type controls protocol and authentication. Pick the one that matches the upstream service before testing or fetching models.
form.baseUrlTooltip: API URL usually ends with /v1. Both http and https are supported, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 or https://api.openai.com/v1
form.connectionSectionHint: Make the channel reachable first, then add keys one by one. In most cases a primary URL plus one working key is enough to continue.

flow.createFlowHint: Fill basics, keys, and models in order. Expand advanced settings only when you need finer control.
flow.createFlowDesc: This dialog keeps the primary path front and center. Make the channel reachable first, then add advanced routing, headers, and overrides.
flow.basicSectionDesc: Set channel name, type, key mode, and key routing policy first.
flow.basicSectionHint: For a normal channel, default mode and default routing are usually enough to start.
flow.keySectionDesc: Add a base URL first, then add usable keys. Source classification and model scope stay in each key's advanced section.
flow.modelSectionDesc: Choose which models this channel should expose. You can add manually or fetch and pick after connectivity is ready.
flow.modelSectionHint: If the base URL or keys are not ready yet, add a small manual model set first and refresh later.
flow.advancedSectionDesc: Proxy, custom headers, match rules, and advanced route overrides live here.
flow.advancedSectionHint: Adjust this layer only when you need to override defaults or add targeted proxy, header, or routing behavior.
flow.baseUrlsDesc: Use one or more base URLs. Keep a primary URL first, and add others only when you need endpoint fallback or delay comparison.

form.testNeedBaseUrlAndKey: Please fill in Base URL and API Key first

form.keyCollapsedReadyHint: The actual API key is already filled in for this entry. Add source classification, remarks, or model scope only when needed.

form.modeSectionHint: Round robin spreads traffic evenly, random spreads quickly, failover fits primary-backup flows, weighted mode fits uneven capacity, and AI dynamic ranks candidates by runtime score.
form.nameHint: Use a stable model family or usage name such as deepseek-chat, claude-code, or embeddings so the default match stays easy to reason about.
form.matchRegexHint: Only fill this when the model names do not line up with the group name, or when you need a more targeted model set.
form.advancedStrategyHint: Open this only when the default mode does not fit your recovery rhythm. Small changes plus runtime observation are usually safer than tuning everything at once.
form.modelPickerTitle: Pick models on the left, confirm order on the right
form.noAvailableModelsHint: Create a channel or sync models on the channel page first, then come back here to keep building this group.

form.retryRoundsHint: Each round walks the current candidate chain again. Larger values add more fallback chances but also increase wait time.
form.retryDelayMsHint: Wait time between retry rounds in milliseconds. Slightly longer delays can help when upstreams flap briefly.
form.failoverWindowSecHint: This window accumulates consecutive failures before the group moves into a more aggressive failover path.
form.raceAfterFailsHint: Parallel race fallback only starts after this many consecutive failures on the same path. Lower values are more aggressive.
form.raceConcurrencyHint: Maximum number of candidates to try in parallel once race fallback starts. Higher values are faster but cost more.
form.firstTokenTimeOutHint: Unit: seconds, only effective for streaming response, 0 = no limit
form.sessionKeepTimeHint: Unit: seconds, keeps using the same channel within a session, 0 = disabled
form.advancedStrategyDesc: Advanced parameters stay folded by default.

aiAutomationSource.title: AI config source
aiAutomationSource.desc: This card is intentionally lightweight. Model fetching, task progress, AI Profiles, and dynamic-routing learning live in the dedicated AI Automation page so Settings stays fast.
aiAutomationSource.noActiveProfile: No AI Profile is active yet. Open AI Automation and choose one first.
aiAutomationSource.profileEmpty: No switchable AI Profile is available yet. Generate one in AI Automation first.
aiAutomationSource.selectedProfilePending: The selected plan is not active yet. It will be activated before AI Profile mode is used.
aiAutomationSource.profileSummaryFallback: No plan summary yet. Open AI Automation to review the task result details.
aiAutomationSource.readyHint: This plan is switchable. Manual config remains intact even after you enable it.
aiAutomationSource.riskDraft: This Profile is still a draft. Review its generated content in AI Automation before switching runtime reads to it.
aiAutomationSource.riskArchived: Archived Profiles are kept for review only. They cannot be activated again.

circuitBreaker.title: Circuit Breaker
circuitBreaker.defaultPathDesc: Check the summary first, then tune only if trips feel too aggressive or recovery feels too slow.
circuitBreaker.advancedDesc: Adjust only the threshold and cooldown budgets here.
circuitBreaker.advancedHint: The defaults already cover most setups. Expand this section only when you see too many false trips, recovery is too slow, or you already understand the upstream limits.
circuitBreaker.recoveryDesc: The current implementation moves between closed, open, and half-open probe states at runtime. You usually do not need to babysit it, but the summary cards below help during noisy incidents.
circuitBreaker.recoveryCompactDesc: Recovery is automatic. Expand the three-step flow only while debugging.
circuitBreaker.recoveryStep1Desc: The same route-target moves into the open state after hitting the failure threshold, and the base cooldown starts counting down.
circuitBreaker.recoveryStep2Desc: After cooldown, only one probe request is allowed through. Parallel requests stay blocked so an unstable upstream does not get flooded again immediately.
circuitBreaker.recoveryStep3Title: 3. A successful probe restores traffic, a failed probe extends cooldown
circuitBreaker.recoveryStep3Desc: A successful half-open probe resets the breaker to normal. If that probe fails, the breaker opens again and keeps extending cooldown with exponential backoff.
circuitBreaker.hint: When a channel reaches the base failure threshold, the circuit trips. Cooldown grows exponentially up to the max cooldown. Runtime tuning can still tighten or relax behavior based on key source type and billing mode.
circuitBreaker.thresholdHint: This is the base threshold. Runtime logic may adjust it further by key source type and billing mode, usually more conservative for paid keys and more tolerant for free or public keys.
circuitBreaker.cooldownHint: The initial cooldown after the first trip. Repeated trips back off to 2x, 4x, and beyond.
circuitBreaker.maxCooldownHint: Upper cap for exponential backoff so one unstable channel does not stay blocked for too long.

recommendation.recommendedTitle: Current values stay near the recommended range
recommendation.recommendedDesc: This range usually works for most traffic: it avoids too many false trips while still stopping a noisy upstream quickly.
recommendation.aggressiveTitle: Current values are aggressive, watch for false trips
recommendation.aggressiveDesc: Very low thresholds or short cooldowns can trip on brief spikes. This only fits upstreams that fail often but recover very quickly, and is usually not ideal for paid channels.
recommendation.relaxedTitle: Current values are relaxed, watch recovery speed
recommendation.relaxedDesc: Very high thresholds or long cooldown ceilings can let unstable upstreams run longer or recover too slowly. Use this only when you already know the upstream rhythm well.
recommendation.currentValues: Current values: threshold {threshold}, base cooldown {cooldown}s, max cooldown {maxCooldown}s.

status.trackedHint: How many route-target breakers are currently tracked in the runtime snapshot.
status.openHint: These targets are still cooling down and will be skipped for now.
status.halfOpenHint: These targets are waiting for or running one recovery probe.
status.cooldownHint: Use this to decide whether to wait a bit longer or move traffic elsewhere first.

dynamicRouting.title: Dynamic Routing Summary
dynamicRouting.description: Control runtime tuning and race budgets.
dynamicRouting.hint: This card owns runtime tuning and race budgets.

learning.title: Local AI learning
learning.hint: Dynamic-routing AI learning is an independent lane that only affects runtime recommendation order.
learning.desc: Settings keeps only the lightweight switch and summary entry. Detailed learning samples, reset controls, and reviews stay in the AI automation center.
learning.switchTitle: Enable local AI learning for dynamic routing
learning.switchDesc: When disabled, existing learning data is retained, but Octopus stops recording new samples and learning no longer participates in scoring.
learning.detailsValue: Review samples, playback, and reset in the AI automation center
learning.summaryEnabledWithSamples: Learning is actively influencing runtime recommendations, and the current samples can reorder candidates in allowed modes such as hybrid.
learning.summaryEnabledNoSamples: Learning is enabled, but no new local samples have been recorded yet. Runtime stays on the mechanism path until real traffic accumulates enough evidence.
learning.summaryDisabledWithSamples: Learning is paused for scoring. Existing samples are kept and can participate again after you re-enable learning.
learning.summaryDisabledNoSamples: Learning is disabled and no samples are stored right now, so dynamic routing ignores learning entirely.
learning.resetFailed: Failed to clear dynamic-routing learning state
learning.resetDisabledHint: There are no learning samples to clear right now.

dynamicRouting.modeHint: Choose whether the recommendation layer only records signals, actively reorders candidates, or forces a conservative mechanism path.

modeDescriptions.shadow-ai: Build a shadow recommendation and audit trail without changing the live request order.
modeDescriptions.hybrid: Adopt the runtime recommendation when confidence is high enough, and automatically fall back when it is not.
modeDescriptions.metrics-only: Compute recommendation metrics and summaries without mutating the active candidate path.
modeDescriptions.strict-mechanism: Use the deterministic mechanism path only. Recommendation ranking is ignored, while existing failover and race mechanisms remain available.
modeDescriptions.incident-safe: Force a conservative emergency posture by tightening live race behavior during unstable periods.

dynamicRouting.defaultPathTitle: Default path: check the switch and summary first
dynamicRouting.defaultPathDesc: Check the switch and summary first, then tune budgets only when needed.
dynamicRouting.healthEnabledHint: The request path uses live health and budget guards when enabled.
dynamicRouting.globalBudgetHint: Caps total race fan-out across the system.
dynamicRouting.groupBudgetHint: Caps race fan-out inside one group.
dynamicRouting.channelBudgetHint: Caps race fan-out for one channel.
dynamicRouting.keyBudgetHint: Caps race fan-out for one key.
dynamicRouting.probeBudgetHint: Caps race fan-out used by probe traffic.
dynamicRouting.budgetSummaryHint: Use this area for a quick scan.
dynamicRouting.budgetSummaryDesc: Review current limits before opening advanced controls.
dynamicRouting.advancedHint: Open only when you need fine-grained tuning.

modelProbe.defaultPathTitle: Review the summary first, then fine-tune by model
modelProbe.defaultPathDesc: Review the summary first, then tune only the models that need it.
modelProbe.defaultPathHint: Probe controls stay here, while pricing stays in the price card.
modelProbe.summaryPolicyHint: The default probe policy currently used by this model.
modelProbe.summaryIntervalHint: The default probe interval. Smaller values make probing more aggressive.
modelProbe.summaryConcurrencyHint: The maximum number of probe attempts this model may run in parallel.
modelProbe.advancedPanelDesc: Only change these three fields when you know a specific model needs a more conservative or more aggressive probe posture.
modelProbe.guidanceTitle: How to choose a probe strength
modelProbe.guidanceHint: Start from the safer default, then only fine-tune the models that truly need it.
modelProbe.guidancePassiveTitle: Keep per-request or high-cost models conservative
modelProbe.guidancePassiveDesc: Start with Passive Only so health checks do not spend extra paid requests just to probe availability.
modelProbe.guidanceSparseTitle: Use sparse single when you need faster recovery checks
modelProbe.guidanceSparseDesc: Sparse single can surface recovery earlier, but it should still keep a longer interval and a low concurrency cap.
modelProbe.guidanceRaceTitle: Reserve sequential or concurrent probing for low-cost targets
modelProbe.guidanceRaceDesc: Sequential and concurrent probing recover faster, but they also create more extra traffic, so they fit free or low-cost targets better.
modelProbe.guidanceCompactDesc: Start from the summary and open models only when needed.
modelProbe.collapsedState: Models stay hidden by default. Search or expand this section only when you need to inspect or change a specific model.

summaryCards.modelCountHint: Counts models in the current search result.
summaryCards.defaultPolicyHint: Shows whether the current result still shares one main default policy.
summaryCards.intervalHint: Uses the first visible model as a quick interval reference.
summaryCards.overrideHint: A channel-level key + model override wins over the model default here.

modelProbe.title: Model Probe Policy
modelProbe.hint: Model probing is separated from price maintenance and managed here centrally.
modelProbe.searchPlaceholder: Search by model or canonical name
modelProbe.empty: No matching models. Try a different keyword.
modelProbe.policyHint: Passive only is the safest default. Sparse single is lighter for health checks, while sequential and concurrent probing recover faster but consume more requests.
modelProbe.intervalHint: Measured in seconds. Lower values probe more often, which can improve recovery speed but increase extra traffic and cost.
modelProbe.concurrencyHint: Caps how many probe attempts for this model can run in parallel to avoid flooding multiple channels at once.
modelProbe.routeOverrideHint: A channel-level key + model override wins over this model default.

doc.title: API Usage Docs
doc.groupNameRule: Group names containing spaces or colons (: / ：) cannot be used in "channel:model" mode
doc.ccswitchIntro: Build an importable CC Switch profile step by step. The screen shows only required fields first, with optional model mappings tucked into an advanced section.
doc.ccswitchAdvancedDesc: Only expand this for Claude when you need separate groups for Haiku / Sonnet / Opus.
doc.ccswitchClientHint: Generate the import profile by client type. Codex appends /v1 automatically, while Claude keeps the raw base URL.
doc.ccswitchKeyHint: The selected API key is embedded into the import link directly. Make sure it can access the target groups.
doc.ccswitchModelHint: This is the main model group. Only open advanced mapping if Claude needs separate Haiku / Sonnet / Opus groups.
doc.ccswitchModelLockedHint: Choose an API key first, then pick the main model group. This avoids showing groups the key cannot use.
doc.ccswitchModelUnavailableHint: The selected API key does not currently expose any importable group. Create or authorize a matching group first.
doc.ccswitchNameHint: Use a clear profile name, such as one based on account or purpose, so it stays easy to switch later.
doc.ccswitchNameLockedHint: Confirm the main model first. The name is then prefilled from the current client and model, and you can still rename it.
doc.ccswitchAdvancedHint: Do not expand this unless needed. Only configure it when different Claude tiers should map to different groups.
doc.ccswitchAdvancedLockedHint: Finish the main model and profile name first, then open advanced mapping only if needed. This keeps the primary import path easy to verify.
doc.ccswitchImportLockedHintKey: Choose the API key first. The import link is generated from that key together with the model selections below.
doc.ccswitchImportLockedHintGroup: The selected API key does not currently expose any importable group. Adjust the key scope or create a matching group first.
doc.ccswitchImportLockedHintModel: Choose the main model group first so the import link can point to the correct primary route.
doc.ccswitchImportLockedHintName: Confirm or rename the profile name first, then you can open the CC Switch import link.
doc.ccswitchProgressHint: Finish the client, API key, main model, and profile name first, then expand advanced mapping only if needed. This is the fastest way to confirm the import link is correct.
doc.ccswitchProgressFootnote: The default path only covers the primary setup. Only expand advanced model mapping when Claude needs separate Haiku / Sonnet / Opus targets.
